title: Can a game of Hex end in a draw?
description: Small Hex boards are filled in different ways to see why one colour always joins its two sides. The video shows that a wall which blocks one player is a chain for the other, and breaks Keeko's doubt that a draw is possible.
teaching_notes: One idea: a wall that blocks one player is itself a winning chain for the other. Watch for students who think both players can be blocked at once.

source: On a 3 by 3 Hex board the players fill all 9 cells. Can the
video_script.why: The child has played Hex and wonders whether a game can end with no winner; trying a small board shows that blocking and winning are the same move.
video_script.substitution: Try to fill a small board so that both players are blocked, and notice that every blocking wall joins the blocker's own two sides.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_6}} and {{NAME_7}} playing Hex on a three by three board of hexagon cells
video_script.wrong_answer: it can end in a draw
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says each player can block the other, so it can end in a draw.
video_script.payoff_line: a full board always has exactly one winner so hex can never end in a draw

final_answer.value: No; a Hex game can never end in a draw
final_answer.spoken: no, a full board always has exactly one winner so Hex can never end in a draw

names.{{NAME_6}}: everyday child, not a character of the book
names.{{NAME_7}}: everyday child, not a character of the book

never_show: the your-turn answer: one player always joins their sides
maths_rules: board: 3 by 3 rhombus of hexagon cells, 3 x 3 = 9 cells
{{NAME_6}} (red) joins the top side to the bottom side; {{NAME_7}} (blue) joins the left side to the right side
a chain is a run of same colour cells, each touching the next along an edge
try 1: blue fills the middle row of 3 cells; that row touches the left and right sides, so it is a blue chain and {{NAME_7}} wins
to stop red going top to bottom, blue cells must cut the board from left to right, and such a cut is a blue chain
a full board always has exactly one winner, so there is no draw
video_script.design: One idea: a blocking wall is itself a winning chain. The wrong idea is that both players can be blocked. The board stays on screen all video.
open_questions: The book does not state that Hex never ends in a draw; the claim comes from the worklist and is a true result for Hex.
